metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Avonmore, PA | Kiski Valley
metaDescription: Avonmore mineral owners in the Kiski Valley: get a plain-English cash offer on your Marcellus royalty, no listing fees, no pressure.
heroLead: Avonmore sits along the Kiskiminetas River, a small Westmoreland County borough where mineral ownership still mostly runs through old farm families.
intro: The Kiski Valley isn't the first place people think of when they picture Pennsylvania's Marcellus boom, but drilling has moved steadily through this part of Westmoreland County over the last decade, and family land around Avonmore has been part of that development. If your family held ground here, there's a real chance a piece of it was leased sometime in the last ten to fifteen years, and a royalty check, however modest, has followed.
We know how it feels to hold a mineral interest and not fully understand what it's actually worth. That's the conversation we want to have before any number comes up.

sections.heading: The Kiski Valley's slower, steadier development
paragraphs: Compared to the intensely drilled counties further southwest, Westmoreland County's Marcellus development has moved at a more measured pace, but it's been consistent, with operators like EQT and CNX active across multiple townships. A family tract near Avonmore may sit in a unit that was drilled more recently than similar acreage in Washington or Greene County, which matters for where the well sits on its production decline curve.
Wet-gas Marcellus production is typical in this area, meaning a real natural gas liquids component and a corresponding post-production deduction on your royalty statement.

sections.heading: A newer well changes the math
paragraphs: If your Avonmore-area well is relatively new, it may still be in its steepest decline period, meaning current royalty income is higher than what it will likely settle into over the next few years. That's an important factor in how we approach valuing a newer interest versus a mature one.

sections.heading: Title work before any number
paragraphs: We confirm ownership through the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds, verify your decimal interest, and review recent statements so any offer reflects where your specific well actually sits in its production life.

faqs.question: Is my well too new to sell?
faqs.answer: No, but timing matters. We factor in where the well sits on its decline curve so the offer reflects realistic future production, not only the current, likely elevated, royalty.

faqs.question: How active is drilling really in the Kiski Valley?
faqs.answer: Less intense than the southwestern core counties, but real and ongoing. We'll confirm the specific activity level tied to your parcel.

faqs.question: What if I only have a portion of the mineral rights, not all of them?
faqs.answer: That's common with older family tracts. We evaluate whatever percentage interest you actually hold, confirmed through title.
